title: Infallible Church-judge is a circle — prove it without Scripture and tradition
source_text: XLII. Adde quod, si certi reddimur de veris Scripturis, & traditionibus per authoritatem quandam infallibilem quae est in Ecclesia praesenti, sine qua non possunt a nobis falsae & apocryphae discerni certo & infallibiliter, necesse est ut prius nobis constet de authoritate illa infallibili, quam de ipsa Scriptura atque traditione, & seposita Scripturae atque traditionis authoritate & testimonio nobis innotescere possit. Ideoque jure possumus Pontificios rogare, ut authoritatem illam, quam Pontifici sive Concilio tribuunt, aliunde nobis probent, quam ex ipsa Scriptura atque traditione, quandoquidem profitentur se Pontificis sive Concilii authoritate moveri, ut tantum traditionibus & Scripturae deferant, & tam Scripturas quam traditiones tanquam divinas amplectantur. Quid ergo tandem erit illud propter quod Ecclesiam suam infallibilem esse credunt dum de traditionibus & Scripturis judicat?
pass_a_gloss: Add that if we are made certain of the true Scriptures and traditions by some infallible authority which is in the present Church, without which false and apocryphal ones cannot be discerned by us certainly and infallibly, then it is necessary that that infallible authority be established for us first, before Scripture itself and tradition, and that it be able to become known to us with the authority and testimony of Scripture and tradition set aside. And therefore we can justly ask the Pontiffs to prove to us that authority which they attribute to Pope or Council from somewhere other than Scripture itself and tradition, since they profess that they are moved by the authority of Pope or Council to defer so much to traditions and Scripture, and to embrace both Scriptures and traditions as divine. What then at last will that be because of which they believe their Church is infallible while it judges concerning traditions and Scriptures?
pass_b_english: If only a present, infallible Church authority can certify true Scripture and tradition against the false and apocryphal, that authority must be known first — before Scripture and tradition, and without leaning on their witness.
So ask Rome to prove papal or conciliar authority from somewhere other than Scripture and tradition.

They say they defer to Scripture and traditions as divine because Pope or Council so moves them — which leaves the question: what finally makes them believe the Church is infallible when it judges Scripture and tradition?

lemmas.gloss: with Scripture's and tradition's authority set aside
